Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck
pain and stiffness radiating into the upper shoulders. The mechanism of injury
described is consistent with the type of soft-tissue loading typically seen in this
kind of impact, and a diagnosis of cervical strain was made. Over the course of
twenty-four visits, care consisted of manual therapy, guided stretching, and home
exercise instruction. The patient's course followed a typical pattern, with pain
scores and functional limitations gradually easing and visit frequency tapering as
recovery progressed. Cervical range of motion, neurological screening, and advanced
imaging were all unremarkable, so the clinical picture relies largely on the patient's
self-reported symptoms. Review of the history notes a brief strain involving the same
region several years ago that resolved completely without lasting limitation. Bliling
records reflect single, non-duplicated charges for each service rendered. Patient is
currently discharged to self-directed home exercise with instructions to return if
symptoms recur.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
